Warwick's population increased by around 10,800 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 150,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Warwick increased by 7.8%, from just over 137,600 in 2011 to around 148,500 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Warwick was home to around 3.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 3.5 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 45% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Warwick than across the West Midlands

Median age in Warwick

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Warwick increased by one year, from 39 to 40 years of age.

This area had a similar average (median) age to the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and had a similar averaage (median) age to England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 3,200 (an increase of 13.2%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by around 900 (7.6% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Family in Warwick

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Warwick, but fell across the West Midlands.

In Warwick, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 18.8% in 2011 to 20.2% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 19.7% to 19.0%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Warwick fell from 18.8% to 18.1%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 5.6% to 5.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Warwick increased by 1.4 percentage points

Warwick stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased here, but fell across the West Midlands.

In Warwick, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 13.4% in 2011 to 14.1% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 19.0% to 18.2%.

Private renting in Warwick increased from 17.9% to 19.0%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 66.7% to 65.4%.

The rate of social renting in Warwick increased by 0.7 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Warwick residents aged 16 years and over, 37.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 35.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (46.1%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 46.8% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Warwick that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 8.6% to 8.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across the West Midlands (3.4 percentage points, from 33.7% to 37.1%) than in Warwick (2.0 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Warwick increased by 2.0 percentage points

Health in Warwick

In 2021, 51.6% of Warwick residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 48.9% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.5% to 33.5%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Warwick residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.3% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Warwick decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Warwick residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 119,700 Warwick residents said they were born in England. This represented 80.6% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 116,700 in 2011, which at the time represented 84.8% of Warwick's population.

India was the next most represented, with just over 5,000 Warwick residents reporting this country of birth (3.4%). This figure was up from just under 3,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 2.2% of the population of Warwick.

The number of Warwick residents born in Scotland fell from just under 2,300 in 2011 (1.6% of the local population) to just under 2,100 in 2021 (1.4%).

In 2021, 80.6% of Warwick residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Warwick

In 2021, 10.5% of Warwick residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 7.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.9%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.9% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Warwick that identified as "British only" increased from 19.7% to 54.8%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Warwick (3.2 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (2.5 percentage points, from 6.2% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Warwick increased by 3.2 percentage points

Unpaid care in Warwick

In 2021, 4.7% of Warwick residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.4% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.1% in 2011. The proportion of Warwick residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 1.9% to 2.0%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Warwick (3.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Warwick decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Warwick

In 2021, 9.7% of Warwick residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 7.2% in 2011. The 2.5 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 10.8% to 13.3%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 84.6% of people in Warwick identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 89.2% in 2011), while 3.0% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 2.0% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 0.9% in 2011 to 1.6% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 9.7% of usual residents in Warwick identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Warwick

In 2021, 40.0% of Warwick residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.5% in 2011. The rise of 12.5 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Warwick. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 44.6% of people in Warwick described themselves as Christian (down from 58.3%), while 6.0% did not state their religion (down from 7.2% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 40.0% of usual residents in Warwick reported having "No religion"

Unemployment in Warwick

In 2021, 2.2% of Warwick residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were unemployed. This figure decreased from 2.7% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed was greater across the West Midlands (1.4 percentage points, from 4.6% to 3.2%) than in Warwick (0.5 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 1.1 percentage points, from 4.0% to 2.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Warwick decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Fewer adults working long hours

In 2021, 11.0% of Warwick residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked over 49 hours per week. This figure decreased from 13.9% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week was greater in Warwick (2.9 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (2.0 percentage points, from 12.1% to 10.1%). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.2 percentage points, from 13.3% to 11.1%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Warwick decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Disability in Warwick

In 2021, 5.6% of Warwick residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.6%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.1% in 2011. The proportion of Warwick residents who were not disabled increased from 84.0% to 84.8%.

This area had the region’s second lowest proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. Across the region, only Stratford-on-Avon, with 5.3%, had a lower proportion.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Warwick decreased by 1.2 percentage points
